title: Impurity-induced Inverse Faraday Effect
authors: A. A. Kopasov, A. A. Bespalov, A. S. Mel'nikov
abstract: We provide a quantum-mechanical description of the photoinduced dc current states and magnetic fields around nonmagnetic point impurities in a two-dimensional (2D) electron gas irradiated by a circularly polarized electromagnetic wave. Based on the solution of the corresponding time-dependent Schrodinger equation within the second-order perturbation theory in the electromagnetic wave amplitude we find that the resulting dc magnetic field component perpendicular to the plane of the 2D system is distributed like in a set of random magnetic fluxes bound to the positions of impurities. As a result, the spatially averaged dc magnetic field does not vanish far from the sample edges and, thus, our scenario of the inverse Faraday effect in disordered systems differs strongly from the standard one based on the relaxation time approximation within the hydrodynamic or kinetic equation approaches which would give only the photoinduced currents flowing along the sample edges. The predicted mechanism for formation of rectified currents flowing around the impurity centers is shown to be generic both for 2D and three-dimensional systems. The internal dc magnetic field can give rise to the photoinduced Hall effect and Faraday rotation for a probing electromagnetic signal.
summary: The paper develops a quantum-mechanical theory for the Inverse Faraday Effect near impurities in 2D electron gases under circularly polarized light. It demonstrates that impurity scattering generates a unique, non-vanishing average magnetic field throughout the sample bulk. This result significantly diverges from classical approaches by incorporating detailed mesoscopic physics into the calculation.
main_problem: The study provides a quantum-mechanical description of photoinduced dc current states and magnetic fields generated around nonmagnetic point impurities in a 2D electron gas when irradiated by circularly polarized light.
main_result: Unlike standard models predicting edge currents, this work shows that the impurity scattering generates a spatially distributed, non-vanishing average dc magnetic field proportional to the impurity concentration ($\langle B_{dc,z} angle \sim n_{imp}$).
method: The analysis involves solving the time-dependent Schrödinger equation using second-order perturbation theory in the electromagnetic wave amplitude.
model_or_system: The system is a two-dimensional electron gas containing nonmagnetic point impurities. The dynamics are governed by the time-dependent Hamiltonian incorporating the impurity potential and the oscillating vector potential from the light field.
key_observables: dc magnetic field component perpendicular to the plane ($B_{dc,z}$), photoinduced dc currents ($\vec{j}_{dc}$), and magnetization ($\vec{M}_{dc}$).
important_parameters: Impurity concentration ($n_{imp}$), electromagnetic wave amplitude ($E_0$), frequency ($\omega$), Fermi energy ($E_F$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on second-order perturbation theory and assumes adiabatic switching of the electric field. It focuses on orbital mechanisms, neglecting spin-orbit effects.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate dc current lines circulating around impurities and the resulting magnetic field pattern; other figures show numerical plots of magnetization, current density, and flux dependence on radius R.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the quantum mechanical framework (Schrödinger equation) to applying second-order perturbation theory. It derives analytical expressions for key observables ($M_z(R)$, $j_\phi(R)$) in both 2D and 3D limits, contrasting these results with standard kinetic/hydrodynamic approaches.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed, microscopic quantum treatment of photoinduced magnetoelectric effects in mesoscopic systems, offering insights into how local disorder can fundamentally alter bulk electromagnetic responses compared to continuum models.
